title.title: Euclidean tensor geometry, and $\omega = 9/4$ exactly
title.subtitle: Claim: over every field, multiplying $n \times n$ matrices costs $n^{9/4}$ up to $n^{\varepsilon}$, no less

plain: Multiplying two tables of numbers: an October paper got the cost down to about $n^{9/4}$; this says it can't go lower

beats.text: The upper bound fell to $9/4 = 2.25$ in October, and humans reproved it
Three wires, one per index, against one shared label per product
Pricing wires as distances in space caps how cheap the shared label can be

steps: Suppose matrices could be multiplied faster than $n^{9/4}$
Then networks of tensors could be compressed again and again
Checking lists for repeats would become too cheap, which is impossible

achievement.label: Open since Strassen (1969)
achievement.note: Every lower bound rests on companion papers from the same unrefereed release

verify.detail: Lean: $\omega = 9/4$ in the division-free model, and VP $\ne$ VNP; not the per-$n$ count
verify.ourCheck: We read the Lean statements; we did not referee the 418 pages

voice.text: The upper bound fell to nine over four in October. This paper claims nothing lower is possible.
A faster method would compress networks so far that a counting bound breaks.
Claimed: omega is exactly nine over four.

sources.quote: 2.371177 (Dupont et al. with AlphaEvolve, arXiv:2608.16884, Aug 2026)
